title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues an axiomatisation of a 'spatios' Σ, defined on the previous page as follows.

- Spat 1: Σ is a complete lattice with bottom 0 and top 1.
- Spat 2: C is an involutive order-reversing bijection of Σ.
- Spat 3: x ∧ Cx = 0.

In modern language Σ is a complete ortholattice, and X|o|Y means X ≤ CY (orthogonality).

**General construction.** Grothendieck starts from an arbitrary set A with a symmetric relation |o|. Let A_00 = {X | X|o|Y for all Y in A}, the elements orthogonal to everything. Define the orthogonal of a subset as orth(B) = {Z | Z|o|X for all X in B}.
- The 'closed' subsets (B = orth orth B) are stable under arbitrary intersections. They therefore form a complete lattice, with smallest element A_00 = orth(A) and largest element A.
- C := orth is an involutive order-reversing map on closed sets, since orth³ = orth by the Galois-connection argument.
- So Spat 1 and Spat 2 always hold.
- Spat 3 (X ∩ orth X = A_00) holds if and only if X|o|X implies X ∈ A_00. He notes this is the condition he had imposed 'dès le début'.

This is the standard polarity / Galois-connection construction: the lattice of orthoclosed subsets of an orthogonality space is a complete ortholattice.

**Test case A = Σ with its own orthogonality.** Here Σ_0 = Σ_00 = {0}. For a subset A of Σ:
- orth(A) = {Z : Z ≤ Inf_{X∈A} CX} = ↓(C Sup A), since Inf C X = C Sup X. So orth A depends only on ξ = Sup A.
- orth orth A = ↓(C C ξ) = ↓ξ.
- Hence the closed subsets are exactly the principal down-sets, and the lattice of closed sets is identified with Σ via ξ ↦ ↓ξ. Complementation corresponds to C.

This is a representation or reconstruction theorem: every complete ortholattice arises as the lattice of closed sets of its own orthogonality relation.

**Margin.** Using Σ* = Σ \ {0} instead gives an anti-reflexive orthogonality, the cleaner notion of orthogonality space. The empty set then becomes a closed set: it is orth(Σ*), corresponding to 0.

**Purpose.** This prepares the next page, where 'figures' of a spatios are introduced: ordered families of pairwise orthogonal nonzero elements. It is part of a pre-geometric axiomatics of 'space' in the 1986 notes.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor slip in notation: the displayed formula writes 'orth A ≝ orth orth A'. It should denote the bi-orthogonal (closure) of A, i.e. a different symbol on the left.

Margin: for A = Σ*, orth(∅) = Σ* and orth(Σ*) = ∅. So ∅ is the smallest closed set, corresponding to 0 = C Sup Σ. The margin's 'à A=∅ correspondrait C Sup ∅ = Σ' should be read as: orth(∅) corresponds to C(0) = 1.

ideas.what: Complete lattice with involutive antitone complementation satisfying x ∧ Cx = 0 ('spatios')
Closed sets of a symmetric relation form a complete lattice with involution; Spat 3 holds iff X|o|X ⇒ X ∈ A_00
ideas.modern_name: orthoclosed subsets of an orthogonality space form a complete ortholattice (polarity / Galois connection)

ideas.what: Every complete ortholattice is recovered as the closed-set lattice of its own orthogonality on Σ (or Σ*)
ideas.modern_name: representation of complete ortholattices by orthogonality spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacLaren (1964), Dacey (1968), folklore in quantum logic

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard facts from quantum logic and lattice theory (orthogonality spaces, complete ortholattices), rederived by Grothendieck for an idiosyncratic axiomatics of 'space'. The only interest is biographical: it shows him in 1986 using quantum-logic-style structures to formalize spatial notions.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is '48' (not '98'). It is consistent with 47 on the previous page and 49 on the next.
'orth A ≝ orth orth A' should be read as (closure of A) ≝ orth orth A = C(Sup C(ξ)) = ξ̃.
'un rapport'/'rapports' at the start and end of the page is uncertain. It possibly refers to the closed subsets ('parties') of A.
